intro: Daily London-session holds (00:00-22:00) on 34 instruments, 2016-10 to 2022, about 1,600 sessions each. Only size varies; 2023 onward is not looked at.

Steadier risk: sizing by the forecast sigma made monthly risk steadier in 34 of 34 instruments (spread of monthly vol 0.19 vs 0.31 unscaled, median). A plain trailing 20-session realised vol does the same (0.19); the forecast beats it in only 15 of 34.

Tails shrink but stay fat: excess kurtosis 2.6 -> 1.9, median worst day -6.4 -> -5.0 sd. Days beyond 3 sd: 0.93% [0.77, 1.09] vs 1.06% unscaled; a normal distribution gives 0.27%. One-day jumps are not forecast. 1/sigma^2 sizing (Moreira-Muir) is worse than both: kurtosis 4.1, 1.41% beyond 3 sd.

The 14-leg book (USD legs as short-USD, gold, indices): equal notional swings from 0.41 to 1.53 of its average vol by year; equal risk 0.74-1.20; equal risk plus a book vol target from the rolling correlation 0.91-1.10. Worst day -9.6 -> -4.1 sd (2020-03-12).

But slow drawdowns do not shrink at equal vol: drift removed, max drawdown -41 (notional), -55 (equal risk), -61 sd (book target); the same days in random order give -29 to -66. Vol sizing trades crash days for a steadier grind.

The book is a few bets: the biggest common factor explains 0.37 (2017) to 0.54 (2022) of its variance vs 0.14 if the legs were unrelated. USD legs average correlation 0.48. Each group's share of risk (USD 47-52%) is close to its share of legs, because the indices are just as much one bet.

Black-Litterman with a zero prior on the real 2021-22 correlation: seven equal short-USD views get 0.015-0.030 per leg vs 0.049 for signal/sigma, and the book's vol falls from 0.27 to 0.10, because the seven views are mostly one dollar view. USDJPY, the least correlated, keeps the most. BL adds no leg that has no view.

Stops: a 1-sigma stop from the open is touched in 29.5% of sessions with the forecast sigma (31.7% for a random walk); 27-31% every year. A constant sigma swings from 25% (2017) to 40% (2022). On days vol came in 1.5-2x the forecast (5% of days) the 1-sigma stop was touched 55% of the time.

charts.title: Steadier risk? Spread of monthly vol per instrument, daily hold
charts.unit: sd of monthly vol (1 = average vol)
charts.note: Each instrument's daily London-session hold, scaled three ways and set to the same average vol. Bar = how much the monthly realised vol wanders around that average (0 = perfectly steady risk). Benchmark: the unscaled bar. Lower = the sizing keeps risk steadier. Direction is irrelevant here; only size moves.

charts.title: Tail days: share of sessions beyond 3 sd, all 34 instruments
charts.note: Each variant at equal ex-post vol per instrument. A day beyond 3 sd is a day that would blow through a 3-sd risk limit. Benchmark: a normal distribution gives 0.27%. Intervals: date-block bootstrap, 2,000 draws.

charts.title: Book realised vol by year (14 legs; 1 = the book's own average)
charts.note: Book = 7 USD legs as short-USD, gold, 6 indices, long. Each book set to sd 1 over 2016-10..2022. A steady book stays on 1 every year. Benchmark: equal notional (indices dominate, 2020 explodes). The book target uses a 60-session correlation, shrunk 30% to its average, from sessions before t only.

charts.title: The book at equal vol: drawdown and tails
charts.note: Same 14 legs, same direction, each book at sd 1 over the window, so only the sizing differs. Benchmark: equal notional. Drawdown also depends on the book's drift (long risk, short USD), so read it next to the tail rows.

charts.title: Book max drawdown at equal vol, with and without its drift
charts.note: As traded, drawdown mixes sizing with the book's drift: equal risk gives the short-USD legs more weight, and the dollar rose in 2021-22, so its drawdown is deeper. With each book's own mean removed, only the path shape is left. Benchmarks: equal notional, and for the drift-removed rows the whiskers are the 5th-95th percentile of the same days in random order (300 shuffles), i.e. what drawdown size is luck of the ordering. A driftless random walk of ~1,550 days at sd 1 expects about sqrt(pi/2 x n) = 49 sd.

rows.label: equal risk + book target, as traded
equal risk + book target, drift removed

charts.title: PC1 share of the book's variance by year
charts.note: Mean of the rolling 60-session PC1 share per year; whiskers = 5th-95th percentile of the rolling values within the year (spread, not a confidence interval). Benchmark: each leg's history shuffled independently, which keeps the vol but removes correlation.

charts.title: Who carries the equal-risk book's risk? Share by group, per year
charts.note: Euler risk contribution (each leg's weight x its covariance with the book) from the shrunk rolling 60-session correlation, sessions before t, averaged over the year. Benchmark: the last row, each group's share of legs (equal risk per leg, so no correlation = these shares). Each group is one bet inside: USD legs average corr 0.476, all 14 legs 0.31.

charts.title: Black-Litterman, zero prior: same 7 short-USD views, real 2021-22 correlation
charts.unit: weight per leg (sigma units, risk aversion 1)
charts.note: Each view: +0.1 sigma tomorrow, short USD on that leg. tau 0.05. Book vol: signal/sigma 0.266, BL 0.103, BL mixed 0.094. Gold and NQ get no view and so get zero weight under BL with a zero prior (He-Litterman: weights are a sum of view portfolios). Benchmark: the signal/sigma bar. BL cuts the legs that repeat the same dollar bet; USDJPY, the least correlated, keeps the most. Illustrative views, no edge claimed.

charts.title: Two equal views (EURUSD, GBPUSD): BL weight on EURUSD vs their correlation
charts.note: Zero prior, each view +0.1 sigma. Benchmark: signal/sigma (flat: it ignores that the two views are the same bet). With He-Litterman omega BL equals signal/sigma at correlation 0 and cuts the EURUSD leg by 20% at 0.5 and 32% at 0.95: two correlated views are partly one view counted twice. Confidence moves the line too: omega x0.25 starts at 1.6x the benchmark, omega x4 at 0.4x.

charts.title: How often a k-sigma stop is touched in the session (long and short, 34 instruments)
charts.note: Entry at the London open, stop k sigma away, held to 22:00. Benchmark: a driftless random walk whose session sd equals sigma touches with probability 2 Phi(-k). Close to the benchmark = 1R means what it says.

charts.title: Does 1R stay 1R? Touch rate of a 1-sigma stop by year
charts.note: Same trades as above at k = 1. If the sigma tracks the market, the touch rate is flat across years (benchmark: 31.7% for a random walk). A constant sigma lets the stop get hit far more in loud years (2020, 2022) and less in quiet ones: the same 1R is a different bet.

charts.title: 1-sigma stop touch rate by how wrong the sigma was (realised 5-min vol / forecast)
charts.note: Realised/forecast is known only after the day: this shows the mechanism, not a rule. Benchmark: 31.7% for a random walk when the sigma is right. Days when vol came in 1.5x the forecast touch a 1-sigma stop most of the time: the stop was really a 0.6-sigma stop.

charts.title: When to cut size? Next-20-session mean daily return of the book after a drawdown
charts.note: Equal-risk forecast-sigma book, drawdown in daily sd from its highest point of the last 60 sessions, in quintiles. Overlapping 20-session windows, date-block bootstrap. Benchmark: the all-days mean. A drawdown throttle only helps if returns after a drawdown are worse than average (momentum in P&L, Kaminski-Lo). The book is a long-risk/short-USD drift, not a strategy.

charts.title: Real days the forecast sigma was far too small (realised 5-min vol >> forecast)
charts.note: A position opened at the London open on the losing side with a 1-sigma stop (dashed). Path in forecast-sigma units, 10-minute samples. Benchmark: on a day the sigma is right the path wanders about +/-1. These are the biggest misses in the window per instrument: the stop is hit early and the move keeps going. Sizing from sigma caps the loss at 1R; it does not make the day small.
